questions.question: What are the main components that make up a basic pinhole camera?
options: A solid glass cylinder with a mirror at one end
An empty, closed box with a tiny hole on the front face and a screen on the back
A convex lens placed in front of a curved piece of black paper
A triangular prism mounted inside a transparent plastic sphere

questions.question: What happens to the image produced by a pinhole camera if you add more holes to the front face?
options: The single image becomes perfectly sharp and bright
Multiple images are produced on the screen
The image flips back to being upright
The image disappears completely because the light cancels out

questions.question: Why does making the pinhole larger cause the image on the screen to become blurred?
options: It blocks all the light except for the green and blue wavelengths
It causes the light rays to bend towards the normal
More light passes through the hole in more directions
It forces the light to travel in curved lines instead of straight lines

questions.question: What does a convex lens do to light rays passing through it?
options: It reflects them backwards at an equal angle to the normal
It refracts them so they travel more towards each other
It splits them into a visible spectrum without bending them
It scatters them in completely random directions

questions.question: How does the refraction of light vary across the surface of a converging lens?
options: Light is refracted more at the edges than near to the centre
Light is refracted only at the exact centre of the lens
Light is refracted equally across all parts of the lens
Light is refracted more near the centre than at the edges

questions.question: If you stand 1.5 metres in front of a flat plane mirror, where does your reflection appear to be?
options: 3.0 metres in front of the mirror, and half your actual size
1.5 metres behind the mirror, and the same size as you
Right on the surface of the mirror, and upside down
0.75 metres behind the mirror, and twice your actual size

questions.question: Why are reflections in a plane mirror described as virtual images?
options: Because they are upside down and much smaller than the actual object
Because they can only be seen when using a green or blue filter
Because they are formed by light rays actually meeting on the surface of the mirror
Because they appear where light rays seem to have come from, not where they actually come from

questions.question: In optical diagrams, how are virtual rays drawn and what do they represent?
options: As solid red lines to show where light is absorbed
As wavy lines to show where light speeds up
As dashed lines to show where light rays appear to have come from
As thick double lines to show where light rays actually cross

questions.question: What color will a white piece of paper appear if it is illuminated only by pure blue light?
options: Blue, because white objects reflect all colours of light
Black, because white objects absorb blue light
Red, because white objects convert blue light into red light
Green, because blue light mixes with the paper's natural yellow pigments

questions.question: Why does a black object appear black when white light shines on it?
options: It reflects only the primary colours of red, green, and blue
It absorbs all colours of light and reflects none
It refracts the light into a hidden spectrum behind the object
It converts all incoming light into virtual rays

questions.question: What happens to the path of a light ray when it enters a transparent glass block from the air at an angle?
options: It bends directly away from the normal
It turns towards the normal
It continues in a straight line without changing direction
It reflects perfectly back along its original path

questions.question: What is the overall effect on the direction of a light ray after it enters and leaves a glass block with parallel sides?
options: It ends up traveling in its original direction, but displaced to the side
It is reflected at exactly 90 degrees to its original direction
It is focused to a single point inside the glass block
It is split into a complete rainbow spectrum that cannot be reunited

questions.question: What is produced when equal amounts of all three primary colours of light (red, green, and blue) are mixed together?
options: Black light
White light
Yellow light
Magenta light

questions.question: Which cells on the retina are responsible for detecting brightness rather than colour?
options: Cone cells
Rod cells
Pixel cells
Prism cells

questions.question: How do modern display screens produce a wide variety of different colours?
options: They physically mix liquid paints behind a clear glass panel
They use tiny red, green, and blue lights (pixels) that vary in brightness
They use miniature triangular prisms that rotate to split white light
They filter light using different thicknesses of gold foil

questions.question: What device can be used to split sunlight into a visible spectrum showing all the colours of the rainbow?
options: A flat plane mirror
A convex converging lens
A transparent triangular prism
A pinhole camera with multiple holes
